entities.summary:
The Battle of Zama was a pivotal event in the Second Punic War, marking the final confrontation between Hannibal and Scipio Africanus in 202 BCE. 

This decisive battle took place in the region of Zama Regia, in present-day Tunisia. It resulted in the defeat of Carthage and the end of the Second Punic War. 

The consequences of the Battle of Zama were far-reaching, as it led to the establishment of Roman dominance in the Mediterranean and the decline of Carthaginian power. 

One of the most enduring legacies of the Battle of Zama is the quote from Polybius, a Greek historian, who wrote: "The battle was fought in a most atrocious manner, and the Romans won a great victory."
